key_insight: DIMAFx is an explainable multimodal framework that learns disentangled modality-specific and modality-shared representations from whole-slide histopathology images and transcriptomics, enabling interpretable cancer survival predictions without sacrificing predictive performance.
problem_solved: Bridges the trade-off between increasingly accurate multimodal survival models and their lack of interpretability by revealing how each data modality and shared signals contribute to survival risk.
method: Disentangled representation learning: separate encoders that extract modality-specific and modality-shared latent factors from WSIs and transcriptomic profiles.
Modality-aware fusion and survival head: combine disentangled factors into a joint predictor (survival loss) while preserving decomposed components for attribution.
Explainability modules: map latent components back to inputs (e.g., heatmaps on slides, gene-level importance) to quantify each modality's contribution to individual predictions.
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy multimodal cancer survival models that are both competitive and transparent, facilitating trust, clinical insight, and targeted hypothesis generation from modality-specific signals.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing separate encoders for images and transcriptomics, disentanglement into shared vs modality-specific latent spaces, fusion, and survival head.
Venn-style or Sankey diagram illustrating how much predictive signal comes from image-only, transcriptomics-only, and shared components.
Example explainability outputs: heatmap overlays on whole-slide images paired with bar plots of top contributing genes for a single patient.
Kaplan–Meier (or survival) curves comparing DIMAFx to baseline multimodal and unimodal models to show maintained or improved performance.
paper_title: Bridging the gap between Performance and Interpretability: An Explainable Disentangled Multimodal Framework for Cancer Survival Prediction
paper_authors: Aniek Eijpe, Soufyan Lakbir, Melis Erdal Cesur, Sara P. Oliveira, Angelos Chatzimparmpas
